newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Le Pen urges Chirac to resign.
newsitem.headline: France's Le Pen urges Chirac to resign.

text.p: French far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen said his National Front had won a major victory in Sundays first round of parliamentary elections and urged conservative President Jacques Chirac to resign.
"President Chirac injected himself personally into the battle. He is defeated, he must leave," Le Pen told supporters.

According to voter surveys, the National Front won between 14.8 percent and 15.3 percent of the first-round vote in the National Assembly election, compared to 12.4 percent in a 1993 general election and 15 percent won by Le Pen himself in a 1995 presidential election.
The surveys predicted the Front would finish with as many as three seats in the assembly, where it now has none, after next Sunday's runoff vote.

The Front "has won a very great victory this evening", Le Pen told supporters in a statement broadcast live on French television. "I urge all voters...to massively mobilise next Sunday so that the National Front can elect enough deputies to enable the voice of France to be heard."

Le Pen declined to say what advice he would give supporters voting in districts where a Front candidate did not survive the first-round vote. Polls show that the Front voters' choices in the runoff could play a decisive role in the election outcome.
